profile.reading: AiNET's Beltsville, Maryland facility, identified by the short code WDC-1 on a dedicated Baxtel industry listing, sits at 11700 Montgomery Road, Beltsville, Maryland 20705, and serves as the company's home base. Founded in 1993 as a dial up internet service provider in Maryland, AiNET has grown into a regional data center, colocation, and fiber network operator serving the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor. The Baxtel listing describes this Beltsville building as a fully operational, single floor facility owned outright by AiNET, certified to SAS 70 Type II and TIA-942 standards, though the listing does not publicly disclose square footage or a specific power capacity figure for this building, restricting that detail behind a paid dataset request rather than publishing it openly. AiNET's own site describes the company's broader footprint as spanning the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor, including its larger CyberNAP facility in Glen Burnie, Maryland, a converted 300,000 square foot former department store roughly 10 miles north of Fort Meade, already on file elsewhere in this registry. No square footage or MW figure could be confirmed for this specific Beltsville building this session despite a fresh attempt, an honest gap rather than a fabricated estimate.
profile.research_note: AiNET publishes only company-wide totals ("400+ MW of capacity," "2,200 on-net global data centers") with no facility-specific spec page found for the Beltsville or Baltimore MD locations.
sources_tried: Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service (1.0 confidence, exact match) cross checked against a dedicated, name specific aggregator listing for this exact facility and a trade press article confirming the operators base city

reading.body:
AiNET's Beltsville facility, identified as WDC-1, sits on Montgomery Road in the Washington-Baltimore corridor as the company's headquarters and serves a region with only three other data centers publishing power specifications, totaling 9.3 MW across Maryland. The operator does not disclose a specific power capacity or square footage for this building on its own site, restricting that detail to paid dataset requests through third-party brokers, so its actual AI hosting potential cannot be assessed from published sources.

The Beltsville building is certified to SAS 70 Type II and TIA-942 standards, qualifying it for secure colocation and enterprise hosting, though the certification alone does not indicate whether it is sized or configured for accelerator-dense AI workloads. AiNET publishes only company-wide totals of 400+ MW across all its facilities globally, making it impossible to know whether Beltsville is a small regional hub or a material piece of that footprint.

Without a published megawatt figure, this campus cannot be ranked against others or assessed as a constraint on AI scaling in the region, placing it among the 11 mapped Maryland facilities but outside the three with disclosed capacity. The absence of a facility-specific spec page is an honest gap rather than a signal of scale.
